result_text:
I fixed the four broken default scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`. The change is uncommitted.

- **HTML pages (pkgdown, Doxygen, meta-generator):** the path pattern was `.*[.](html|html|xhtml)`, a typo that repeated `html` and dropped `htm`. It is now `.*[.](htm|html|xhtml)` on all three rules.
- **.NET `<doc>` XML and `// Generated by` JavaScript:** the path patterns were `.*/[.]xml` and `.*/[.]js`, which need a literal `/.xml` or `/.js` filename. They are now `.*[.]xml` and `.*[.]js`.
- **Gradle JavaScript:** the build-and-deployment pattern was `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js`, which needs a literal `.-gradle.js`. It is now `.*[-]gradle[.]js`.

The content patterns are unchanged, so an ordinary `.htm`, `.js` or `.xml` file still needs its generated-code marker to match. `build.gradle` still matches the existing `.*[.]gradle` rule.

`mvn -o -pl codeanalyzer test` ran, and every surefire report shows zero failures and zero errors. No existing test covers these conventions, so nothing checks the new matches. I tried a scratch check of the regexes against sample filenames, but writing to `/tmp` was blocked by a permission prompt, so that check did not run.
